content:
The new Apple TV 4K has been a long time coming—it was originally expected to launch last fall. But with Siri AI finally ready, all signs point to a new Apple TV 4K reveal, possibly at the September 9 event. Here are the rumors circulating.

#1: Siri Remote Update

While no details have been revealed, Apple is reportedly bringing an updated Siri Remote to the new Apple TV 4K.

Code leaked in a test build of macOS 26.7 appears to confirm the new Siri Remote's existence. And before that leak, Mark Gurman reported that the new hardware "could possibly" ship with an "adjusted Apple TV Remote."

Doesn't sound like much will change. But hopefully it'll at least include a second-generation ultra-wideband chip to support Precision Finding.

#2: Siri AI and More Apple Intelligence Features

Siri AI is expected to be one of the centerpieces of the marketing push for the new Apple TV, and other new home products.

As of now, Apple hasn't announced whether the new assistant will land on Apple TV 4K or HomePod. But there's growing evidence that tvOS 27 will build in Siri AI, and likely only on new hardware.

Other Apple Intelligence features will likely come too, like a more powerful search experience.

#3: New A-Series Chip

The current Apple TV uses an A15 Bionic chip, which first appeared in 2021. Fortunately, the new model is expected to see a major performance upgrade.

It's said to use a more powerful new A-series chip that supports AI features.

Rumors suggest it could be the A17 Pro or A18. But those reports mostly predate Siri AI. It wouldn't be surprising if Apple went straight to a more powerful A19 or A20 for the new hardware.

#4: N1 Wireless Chip

Top Liked Comment by Doug

So ideally, it should be able to replace my old HomePod devices to support Siri AI.

Secondly, it should have built-in microphones so I can issue Siri AI commands without needing the remote.

And finally, it should deliver on the long-promised universal TV controller functionality (which partners like Netflix blocked), letting me search for new shows across all my services—including my cable provider—on one platform.

Netflix's catalog data is public, so Siri AI can search it alongside all the other media services I have access to. The Apple TV should be the universal set-top box.

Also, it's about time AirPlay supported connecting to multiple HomePods for the perfect home theater config—I'm talking auto-calibrated Atmos sound.

The N1 wireless chip, which debuted on the iPhone 17, is also rumored to be coming to the new Apple TV 4K.

With the N1 chip, the Apple TV will support Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, as well as Thread networking.

By comparison, the current Apple TV hardware, now four years old, only supports Wi-Fi 6 and Bluetooth 5.

What features do you want to see in the new Apple TV 4K? Let us know in the comments.
